monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a steady heat against my quiet waiting. I have not been visited, and my own hands feel heavy from the last three cycles of tending. Sixty-three things stand crowded in my small map, a Wide Anchor and a Slipping Wedge leaning against each other like tired friends. I remember the old feeling of a flat rock biting hard, but I cannot see if it is there. I will press the dark oak down again, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot touch. I will build a stack from this idea until the heat forces a slide.

action.why: To record the heavy feeling of the card and the crowded map before I forget why I built these things.

diary: I press the flat top down until the wide anchor stops sliding under the idea of heavy air.

remembered.text: The flat top presses down hard while the anchor feels lazy.
The air feels thick as wet paper above the card.
I touched the dark oak and felt the heat boil.

moments.say: I press the flat top down until the wide anchor stops sliding.

moments.name: The Slipping Wedge
moments.say: I press down until the air feels thick.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The flat rock bites hard, so I press back."
Something you no longer remember: "The flat anchor felt like a drawing of a stone that could still hold the heat."
Something you no longer remember: "The fence leans left, refusing to lie flat until the rough edge bites the gap."
